summary: Attempt 2 fixes the two review findings sent back to this stage and nothing else. For B1 (O-003), TopLevelRowText.cs no longer names the Store namespace. TopLevelRow in Core now has `IsFolder => Kind == EntryKind.Folder`. FiguresOf tests `!row.IsFolder`, and the `using FsAnalyser.Core.Store;` line is gone. For R2-m1 (O-004), TryUsedBytes also refuses a difference above long.MaxValue, and the HF-024 test now asserts that (ulong.MaxValue, 0) is no figure. Build, full suite (394), the SL-063 bug test and a report-mode run of the published exe all pass, and a check of every .taad/fitness.yaml pattern finds no new hit.

files.why: B1/O-003: adds `public bool IsFolder => Kind == EntryKind.Folder;` to TopLevelRow, so the window can ask whether a row is a folder without naming the store's EntryKind. (Attempt 1 changes, now committed: TopLevelKind deleted, Kind is EntryKind.)
B1/O-003: FiguresOf tests `!row.IsFolder`, and `using FsAnalyser.Core.Store;` is deleted. Relative to the base commit, the file differs only in the comparison line.
R2-m1/O-004: TryUsedBytes' guard is `free > total || total - free > long.MaxValue`, and its doc says why.
R2-m1/O-004: AFreeFigureAboveTheQuotaTotalIsNoFigure also asserts `Assert.False(Kernel32.TryUsedBytes(ulong.MaxValue, 0, out used))`, and its doc covers the second bound.

obligations.how: I made the review's smallest fix. TopLevelRow.IsFolder was added in Core, TopLevelRowText.FiguresOf uses `!row.IsFolder`, and the Store using is deleted. I grepped every App .cs file outside FolderTree*.cs: no other file compares a TopLevelRow's Kind (KindRowText's k.Kind and MainWindow's outcome.Kind are other types), and no .xaml maps clr-namespace:FsAnalyser.Core. I ran the rule's three patterns (\bScanStore\b, (?<!\bresult)\.Store\b, \bStore\s*:) over the same files: 0 hits. The snapshot-immutability patterns on TopLevelSnapshot.cs: 0 hits. fitness.yaml was not changed.

TryUsedBytes now refuses `free > total || total - free > long.MaxValue`. The case test asserts (ulong.MaxValue, 0) returns false, and keeps the quota case and the ordinary subtraction (626 GiB - 100 GiB = 526 GiB). It passes: `--filter FullyQualifiedName~FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.VolumeUsageTests.AFreeFigureAboveTheQuotaTotalIsNoFigure`, 1 passed. I did not rerun the new assert against the old guard. The old code returned (long)(ulong.MaxValue - 0) = -1 with true, which the review confirmed in the tree.

deviations: Correction to attempt 1's account: it said the fitness patterns for the edited files all still held. That was wrong. I had checked only the Core rules, and the SL-039 App rule 'the window never touches the scan store' was broken by the Store using in TopLevelRowText.cs. This attempt removes that crossing, and I ran every rule's patterns over the tree instead of a hand-picked few (see tests).
Carried over from attempt 1, unchanged: the ScanOptions.ListedFileId test seam (HF-001), the 'no file lacked an ID' rule (HF-001), and LongPath.ToDisplay over dropping prefix handling (HF-011).
not_built: HF-024's 'better' fix is not built, as in attempt 1: both figures from one quota-independent source (GetDiskSpaceInformationW or FileFsFullSizeInformation). The guard now refuses both wrap-around bounds, but a quota above the volume's free space still gives a positive, mixed figure.
HF-005: links were removed from ScanProgress rather than shown in the counters line, as in attempt 1.

tests.note: Full default suite: 394 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 23 s, including RuleCopiesAgreeTests (eng/rules-parity.ps1).
Bug catalog: 10 passed. It drives TopLevelRowText through the real App converter.
C-002 / O-004 case: 1 passed, with the new ulong.MaxValue/0 assert.

A throwaway stdlib reader of .taad/fitness.yaml, deleted afterwards. The TAAD Fitness tool and harness.py are not available here, and there is no PyYAML. It read all 62 rules and matched every must_not_match pattern against whole-file text in each rule's files/except_files scope. Comments were not stripped and must_not_import was ignored. One hit in a changed file: TopLevelTracker.cs:14, the pre-existing doc comment 'takes a lock (SL-039)', matched by `\block\s*\(` on a rule without including_comments. That line predates this slice and the engine strips comments for such rules. The other hit is in a file this slice did not touch. No hit in TopLevelRowText.cs. Not the engine's own Fitness op=check, which the next gate runs.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 publish src/FsAnalyser.App/FsAnalyser.App.csproj -c Release -o artifacts/publish
tests.note: Published the single-file exe to the gitignored artifacts/publish.

EXIT 0, 'Finished: C:\Windows\System32\drivers', Completed: 659 files, 11 folders, 0 links, 242,585,339 bytes, the same figures as attempt 1's run. No file-ID note. I did not repeat attempt 1's whole-drive C:\ run (8 min 20 s, positive volume figure): this attempt changes only a guard branch that a real volume under 8 EiB never takes.

follow_ups: HF-024 residual, as in attempt 1: a per-user quota above the volume's free space still gives a positive but mixed used figure (quota total less volume free). A quota-independent source (GetDiskSpaceInformationW's Actual* allocation units, or FileFsFullSizeInformation) would fix it, after re-measuring against Get-Volume.

The SL-039 App store rule (`(?<!\bresult)\.Store\b`) has no xUnit twin, so `dotnet test` stays green when it breaks, which is how attempt 1 missed it. It also forbids App files outside FolderTree*.cs from naming the EntryKind enum, not only from reading a store. A person may want to decide whether an enum import should be allowed, or whether the rule should get a twin in ArchitectureRulesTests.
HF-001: MainWindow's note still says 'This drive does not report file IDs', though with the value-based flag it can also show when only some files lacked an ID.
